title: I Took the Theremin-Booth Hours to the Host Who Left My Numbered Antenna

parts.text: I stepped into booth three at 7:02 p.m. and host Niall was already using numbered gear. The board said: ONE BOOTH. FORTY-FIVE MINUTES. ANTENNAS STAY WITH THE BOOKING. I was twenty-seven, booth secretary, holding a clipboard that listed our numbered antenna. Niall shrugged. "Hosts are the field." I photographed the board, the booking, and his leftover volume loop on my numbered antenna. Then I asked for the field log. At 7:10 the desk pinged why Niall's name was on my loop. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The desk can see Niall's leftover volume loop on my numbered antenna.

social.video_title: He left my numbered theremin antenna on my booth — Part 1/2
social.description: Theremin booth, leftover volume loop, a forty-five-minute clock he posted. I logged the field. Would you have asked for the field log?

parts.text: Niall called it pitch hunting until the desk asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the board, and the loop still. The antenna went back to my numbered booking. Niall ran a slot of his own and told the next host atmosphere was always about optics. Optics is a word people use when a booking exists. Policy now has a second line: HOSTS ARE NOT THE FIELD. I keep my antenna on a labeled stand. Niall brown-bags his hunting. The booth finally looks like a booking, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.video_title: Hosts are not the field — Part 2/2
social.description: Field log, numbered antenna, and a second line on the board. Was pitch hunting ever my loop?
